correctness.rationale: Convolution gives T_t(r)=e^(−t)[r e^(−t/r)−e^(−tr)]/(r−1), with equal/sparse limits e^(−2t)(1+2t) and e^(−t). Direct differentiation reduces derivative sign to h_t; on x=t(r−1) below critical 1−u sign equals that of L_t(x), whose exact derivative factors as x²[(t−1)x²+t(2t−3)x+t²(2t−3)] /[(t+x)²(1+x)(t−(t−1)x)]. For t≥3/2 all coefficients nonnegative so strict increasing weight imbalance; for 1<t<3/2 the quadratic has exactly one positive root giving one interior strict minimum. Endpoint comparison gives tau unique in (1,3/2). Independently checked both derivative identities symbolically (residual zero), endpoint and dense grid examples t=1.05,1.2,tau,1.35,1.499,1.5,2; finite grid only corroborates the analytic sign proof.
residual_risks: Only t>1, 2 iid exponentials and nonnegative weights; strict-positive weights remove attainment at sparse endpoint.

evidence: Classical Schur-type tail inequalities yield extrema in certain far-tail regions. They do not automatically cover the intermediate interval 1<t<3/2 with a unique interior minimizer and the separate endpoint height crossing tau.
